notes: DRAFT RUBRIC. Every numeric range below is a placeholder and MUST be reviewed and signed off by a subject matter expert before it is used to grade real students.
Angles are joint angles in degrees: the angle between the two listed segments measured at the joint. 0 = fully folded, 180 = straight.
Entries with unit 'ratio' are dimensionless proportions, not degrees.
No pose-estimation model runs in this app. A vision-language model ESTIMATES these angles from a single photograph, so values are approximate and must never be presented as measurements.
To finish an entry: confirm ideal_min / ideal_max / tolerance, add a reviewer_note explaining the source, then set verified to true.
To add a pose: copy an existing entry, give it a unique id, and rebuild its angles list. No application code changes are required.

asanas.name: Tadasana
asanas.camera_hint: Front view. Whole body in frame, head to feet, feet fully visible.
asanas.summary: An upright standing pose. The whole body stacks vertically over the feet: ankles, knees, hips, shoulders and ears in one line.

angles.label: Left knee extension
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Confirm the accepted hyperextension allowance for a beginner.

angles.label: Left hip extension
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Tight hamstrings will pull this below range; decide whether that is an error or a modification.

angles.label: Left elbow extension (arms alongside body)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Assumes the classic arms-at-sides variation, not arms overhead.

angles.label: Trunk lean away from vertical
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Small leans are common; decide how strict this should be for a beginner.

angles.label: Stance width (distance between ankles / hip width)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Covers 'feet together' through 'hip width'; confirm the intended variation.

qualitative_cues: Weight even across both feet, through the tripod of each foot
Kneecaps lifted, thighs engaged without locking
Ribs knit, chest broad, shoulders relaxed away from the ears
Chin level, gaze soft, crown of the head lifting
common_mistakes: Pelvis tipped forward (anterior tilt) with ribs thrusting
Weight rolled onto the outer edges of the feet, arches collapsing
benefits: Strengthens the legs, ankles and core
precautions: Low blood pressure or dizziness: take a wider stance and keep the gaze steady
Balance concerns: practise near a wall
Recent knee or ankle injury: keep a microbend in the knees
references: Light on Yoga (B. K. S. Iyengar) — Tadasana

asanas.name: Virabhadrasana II
asanas.camera_hint: Front view, square to the mat. Both feet, both arms and the whole torso in frame.
asanas.summary: A wide standing pose with the front knee bent toward ninety degrees, the back leg straight, torso upright over the hips, and both arms extended parallel to the floor.

angles.label: Left knee flexion (assumes left leg forward)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Knee tracking over the ankle matters more than the exact number; confirm both.

angles.label: Right knee extension (back leg)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Some traditions allow a slight bend; decide which line the rubric grades.

angles.label: Left hip flexion (front leg)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Depends heavily on the depth of the lunge; may need widening.

angles.label: Right hip extension (back leg)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Hip flexor tightness is the usual limiter.

angles.label: Left shoulder abduction (arm parallel to floor)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. This is the arm-elevation angle; confirm it matches your teaching cue.

angles.label: Right shoulder abduction (arm parallel to floor)
Trunk lean away from vertical
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Leaning over the front thigh is a common error; decide the threshold.

angles.label: Stance width (ankle-to-ankle / shoulder width)
angles.reviewer_note: Placeholder. Depends on the student's leg length; may need to be a per-student range.

qualitative_cues: Front knee tracks in line with the second toe, not collapsing inward
Back leg firm, outer edge of the back foot grounded
Torso upright over the pelvis, ribs stacked over hips
Both arms in one line, parallel to the floor, shoulders away from the ears
common_mistakes: Front knee collapsing inward or travelling past the ankle
Front thigh not approaching parallel to the floor
Torso leaning forward over the front leg
Back heel lifting or back knee bending
Arms drifting below shoulder height, shoulders hunched
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the legs and ankles
precautions: Knee injury: reduce the lunge depth and keep the front knee above the ankle
High blood pressure or heart conditions: keep the gaze level rather than up
Neck strain: keep the head in line with the torso
Groin or hip injury: shorten the stance
references: Light on Yoga (B. K. S. Iyengar) — Virabhadrasana II
